tools.description: Resolve every open choice in the current spec deterministically (parts, dimensions) and replace the current design; then runs every check and returns the report.
tools.name: design

tools.description: Make the best design verified so far (fewest failing checks including regression cases, then the best objective) the current design again, and run every check. Use it when your changes made things worse.
tools.name: revert_best

tools.description: Change the resolved design by RFC 7396 merge patch, e.g. swap a part id or a dimension. Must stay a valid design. Run check afterwards.

patch_json.description: merge patch as a JSON object string

tools.name: edit_design

tools.description: Read-only lookup of the catalog rows a design choice can take (id, label, key specs, price, stock, url). Call it before putting any part id into edit_design: never guess an id. With path "" it lists which design paths are catalog-backed. Changes nothing.

path.description: dotted design path of the choice, e.g. "structure.boom_tube"; "" to list the catalog-backed paths

query.description: text to match in the id or label, e.g. "carbon 16mm"; "" for no filter

tools.name: catalog

tools.description: Ranked, read-only search of the catalog rows at one design path, filtered by text, numeric spec ranges and stock, each row with why it matched. Rows you can buy today rank first, then the closest text match, then price. Use it to find a part by attribute (a lighter motor, a stiffer tube) instead of scanning the catalog listing.

path.description: dotted design path of the choice, e.g. "propulsion.lift_motor"; "" to list the catalog-backed paths

query.description: text to match in id, label or any spec; "" for none

ranges.description: numeric spec ranges, comma separated, `attr:min..max` with either bound optional, e.g. "kv:800..1200, mass_g:..60"; "" for none; the spec names are the keys shown by catalog

sort.description: lead with one spec, e.g. "mass_g" ascending, "-kv" descending, "price"; "" for the default ranking

stock.description: which stock states to return: in_stock only; listed (in stock or priced with no stock line; the default and the spec's usual stock policy); lead_time adds made-to-order/pre-order/backorder; restock adds out of stock. Discontinued rows never return

tools.name: catalog_search

tools.description: Read-only: every other catalog row that can take the same role as the current (or a named) part at a design path, with a delta table of every spec that differs (from -> to, percent) and the price change, best first (stock, then fewest differences, then smallest price change). Use it before swapping a part to see what you would give up.

id.description: the incumbent id to compare against; "" for the current design's choice at that path

path.description: dotted design path of the choice, e.g. "propulsion.lift_motor"

tools.name: alternates

tools.description: Read-only: the bill-of-materials diff between the best verified design (the incumbent) and the current design: lines added, removed and changed with each line's cost delta, the total before and after, unpriced lines, and any part the current design brings in that is not in stock. Call it after edit_design to see what a swap costs before you check.
tools.name: bom_diff

tools.description: Run every declared check (plus every confirmed regression case) on the current spec and design. Returns each margin with its unit and source; missing evidence fails.
tools.name: check

tools.description: The bill of materials: every line with price, vendor URL and the total. Unpriced lines are errors.
tools.name: bom

tools.description: Use the shared persistent native FreeCAD document. Units mm/degrees. For coupled dimensions prefer bind_parameters:{bindings:[{object_name,parameter,source_object,source_parameter,scale:1,offset_mm:0},...]}: 1..128 unique typed targets are applied atomically with one recompute/validation and full rollback on failure. No arbitrary expression strings. Start complex CAD discovery with inspect:{summary:true,offset:0,limit:100}; this returns a lightweight paginated object/dependency list and does not verify geometry. Then inspect:{objects:[names]} for current geometry and dimensions of only the features you need, including construction features and shared dimensions. Follow dependency names to inspect deeper as needed. Avoid full inspect:{} unless the complete geometry tree is necessary. Results include editable_parameters and assembly containers. For motors, propellers, PCBs/flight controllers and ESCs, prefer suitable off-the-shelf parts and query component_catalog first. component_catalog:{query} lists exact local manufacturer CAD identities and availability; query may be an explicitly mapped BOM catalog ID. Before inserting a model as selected real hardware, its exact identity and source provenance must match the resolved BOM. If exact CAD is unavailable, report the gap; any envelope or proposed alternative must be separately labeled and must not silently replace the selected component. import_component:{component_id,name,position:[x,y,z],axis:[x,y,z],angle_degrees:0} verifies the catalog hash and imports that exact model with provenance. It does not select a replacement in the aircraft BOM; unavailable exact models remain unavailable. Preserve the supplier coordinate frame and use explicit placements: mounting_frame_verified:false means no mounting datum or automatic alignment is established, so do not infer a mount from bounding-box centers. Do not resize or relabel a different motor, propeller or flight controller to impersonate the selected part. import_step: {path,name,position:[x,y,z],axis:[x,y,z],angle_degrees:0} imports actual local STEP solids as separately placeable native BREP snapshots, preserves source hash and matching labels, and uses file-derived units normalized by OCC: SI mm/cm/m and audited inch/foot conversion graphs, including mixed per-representation contexts. No caller unit override; unknown, cyclic or inconsistent unit graphs are rejected. Import defaults remain 50 MiB and 512 entities; explicit integer max_source_mib:1..200 and max_entities:1..4096 may raise those requested budgets, while the 100000-face cap remains. Both import actions support preserve_labels:false to skip the optional second supplier STEP read for matching labels; default true preserves existing behavior. Source entity indices, source hash and native geometry remain retained; labels_status:not_requested explicitly reports absent recovered labels. Prefer summary:true for large imports: full validation still runs, but detailed object records are omitted; physical/reference names, counts, unit/source provenance and requested budgets remain, with a 512 KiB summary limit. Use paginated/scoped inspect afterward. Non-solid geometry is rejected by default. import_component/import_step may explicitly set preserve_reference_geometry:true to retain supported shells/faces as reference-only objects alongside solids; object_names lists physical solids and reference_object_names lists preserved surfaces. Reference surfaces have no mass/collision-solid claim; check geometry_coverage for omitted same-import surfaces. Native checkpoints preserve all geometry, but checked STEP save rejects any selection from a mixed import instance. render may explicitly include reference_objects:[names]; omission from rendering or physical checks must not be described as complete source coverage. Source history and PCB electrical connectivity are not imported; inspect returned object_names, place/check/save them. open_document: {path} opens an existing FCStd into an empty session; later checkpoints go to this run, preserving the source file. make_parameters: {name,parameters:{Gap:{value:12,min:1,max:30}}} creates shared dimensions in mm. Native Part::Mirroring also permits binding Base.x, Base.y, or Base.z plane-origin coordinates (not other object types); for example bind_parameter:{object_name:LiftRRMotor,parameter:Base.x,source_object:RearRotorLayout,source_parameter:RearMotorX,scale:0.5,offset_mm:52.5}. bind_parameter: {object_name,parameter,source_object,source_parameter,scale:1,offset_mm:0} binds a native editable dimension or Placement.Base.x/y/z to a shared dimension using a linear expression; then edit the shared source with set_parameter. boolean: {name,operation:cut|fuse|common,base,tool} creates a new native editable boolean from two distinct existing physical single solids; use a new result name. Empty/invalid results, no-effect cuts/fuses and disconnected fuses fail transactionally. Export final result only, not its construction operands. For a cut using an actual mating component, explicitly pass retain_tool_as_part:true; that mating tool may then be exported with the result only when their material does not overlap. mirror: {name,source,normal:[0,1,0],origin:[0,0,0]} creates a linked physical instance reflected across a plane; edit source dimensions to update both sides. Source and mirror may both be checked/exported; connectivity and collisions still require check. convert_spline_loft: {source,name,split_index,sampled_tolerance_mm} creates a separately named native spline loft from an existing solid ruled polygon-section Part::Loft without retyping coordinates. Source is preserved. Supports line-only Wright sections and copies supported shared-dimension section translation expressions; source coordinate edits are NOT associative. Records source geometry hash and snapshot provenance. Use explicit split and sampled tolerance, then inspect/check new outputs; not exact polygon equivalence or a certified continuous deviation bound. make_part: {spec:{name,kind,params}}; kinds box{x,y,z}, cylinder{radius,height}, tube{radius,bore_radius,height}, mount{x,y,z,bores:[[startXYZ,endXYZ,radius],...]}, loft{rings:[closed XYZ polygons]}, spline_loft{rings,split_index,sampled_tolerance_mm,ruled?:boolean} uses optional strict boolean ruled defaults true; false requests smooth native spanwise interpolation and requires renewed wall/interference checks (section sampled tolerance is not a 3D wall guarantee). Two interpolated native B-splines per closed section: 2-16 corresponding sections, 8-256 points per section, total <=2048, split leaves >=4 points on each branch, 0<tolerance<=1 mm. Tolerance measures sampled curve-to-source-polyline deviation, not a certified continuous bound. loft_shell{rings,inner}, extruded_skin{profile:[XYZ vertices],direction:XYZ,wall}, profile_plate{profile_object,direction:XYZ,thickness,bores} (links to an existing skin cavity profile). set_profile: {object_name,points:[XYZ vertices],summary:true} edits a constrained native sketch section, preserving spline type and provenance; inspect names first. set_profile and set_parameter summary:true keep full native validation/rollback but return compact edit metadata and dependent-name candidates; these are not contact checks. Scoped-inspect final physical outputs and run check after edits. Omit summary for legacy full document descriptions. set_parameter: {object_name,parameter,value,summary:true}; native properties Length/Width/Height or Radius/Height, extrusion LengthFwd, inward profile offset Value (negative), and supported Rocket tube Length/Thickness/AxialOffset (signed); only use names listed in editable_parameters. place: {object_name,position:[x,y,z],axis:[x,y,z],angle_degrees}; direct place is unavailable for assembly-controlled Rocket components. analyze_wing: {object_name,velocity_m_s:20,alphas_deg:[0,4,8],altitude_m:0,samples_per_branch:65,symmetric:true} runs the fixed open-source AeroSandbox/OptVL cross-check and separate NeuralFoil section polar analysis on actual current native two-branch spline-loft sections. Select a supported solid spline loft, often the outer construction loft, not a skin Boolean. Limits: velocity 1..100 m/s; 1..5 unique finite alphas in -10..12 degrees; altitude 0..20000 m; integer samples 33..129; strict boolean symmetric (right half-wing root must be at Y=0). Output directory is managed. Read-only: returns bounded numeric summary plus JSON/PNG/CSV artifacts, source geometry/runner hashes, mesh convergence and cross-solver comparison. Solvers approximate smooth spanwise CAD between sampled sections; symmetry is an assumption, and section polar confidence is not whole-wing stall proof. Do not claim full-aircraft stability, rotor-wash effects, structural integrity or flight readiness from this wing-only result. check_containment: {container:name,contents:[names],minimum_clearance_mm:0} measures actual solid containment and distance to all container boundary shells, allowing valid one-solid construction objects. Boundary distance is not clearance when contained:false; inspect per-object outside_volume/contained/clearance_passed and coverage. For wall clearance use the outer solid as container and cavity solid as content; for component fit use the cavity solid as container. It is read-only and does not prove load rating or manufacturing readiness. check_translation: {moving:[names],obstacles:[names],translation:[dx,dy,dz],samples:11} screens a straight removal/insertion path: clear only if conservative swept bounds prove no penetration, blocked if an actual sampled collision exists, otherwise inconclusive. It does not solve assembly joints or cable/tool access. check: {objects:[names],contacts:[[a,b],...],tolerance_mm:0.1,require_connected:true,summary:true}; summary computes all pairs but returns only clash and declared-contact pair details plus total counts/components; omitted pairs are not untested, and full evidence remains available in saved geometry-check.json. Omit summary or use false when every pair detail is needed. Prefer summary for large assemblies. Use require_connected for a single assembly; geometric connectivity is not a load-bearing joint verification. Declared contacts never exempt penetration. render: {objects:[final physical names],width:640,height:480,azimuth_degrees:35,elevation_degrees:25,deflection_mm:0.5,max_triangles:100000,angular_deflection_radians:0.35} uses optional angular_deflection_radians in 0.05..1.0. Render defaults remain max_objects:128 and max_source_faces:20000; explicit budgets may raise these to 4096 and 100000, but existing 100000-triangle and pixel/work caps still apply, so use scoped selections when full rendering fails. It returns a bounded native B-rep raster image with geometry fingerprint metadata; inspect the image together with native measurements, not as proof of fit or hidden geometry. save_preview: {objects:[physical names],reference_objects:[reference names],max_objects:512} writes an editable native document and GLB preview with explicit physical/reference counts and visible geometry_role metadata; it does not produce STEP or claim roundtrip_valid. The preview object budget defaults to 512 and may explicitly be set to an integer up to 4096. Include all intended reference objects and inspect preview_coverage for omissions. Use it to display mixed manufacturer geometry in the project without weakening checked export. save: {objects:[final physical output names]}; directory managed by the run. Native helper objects are not extra assembly parts. CAD edits do not automatically change the resolved domain design, flight checks or BOM; reconcile them explicitly. A passing CAD fit check is not manufacturing or flight approval.

args_json.description: Action parameters as a JSON object string; no Python code

tools.name: cad_action

tools.description: Design of experiments on the current design, read-only: for 1 to 3 design parameters, evaluate every check (including regression cases) at each point of a grid (or a Latin hypercube with 3 parameters or a grid over the point cap) and return a table with each point's passing count, failing checks and objective headlines, plus the Pareto front among the best points. Writes a CSV and an SVG plot under the run's sweeps/. Changes nothing: pick a point from the table and apply it with edit_design, then check. Bounded to 200 points and 20 s.

max_points.description: cap on evaluated points, 1-200; 60 is plenty for a first look

maximize.description: headline labels to maximize in the Pareto front; [] keeps the defaults (the domain objective, and each headline by its own bound)

minimize.description: headline labels to minimize in the Pareto front; [] keeps the defaults

params_json.description: JSON object string: design path -> range. A path is dotted ("envelope.balloon_g") or a JSON pointer ("/envelope/balloon_g"). A range is a list of values ([600, 800, 1200] or part ids) or {"min": 0.8, "max": 2.0, "steps": 7}. 1 to 3 paths, e.g. {"envelope.balloon_g": [600,800,1000], "envelope.fill_target_mps": {"min":4,"max":6,"steps":5}}
